subject: Intermittent packet fragmentation & routing failures to Helios private deployment
messages:
From: Sam Carroll <sam.carroll@helioshealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: netops@helioshealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

Hi Irene / Dev team,

We started seeing intermittent failures this morning from our on-prem app cluster to the Redwood Private connector in us-west-2. Symptoms: long-lived TCP sessions show bursts of retransmits and several connections reset after ~60s. We've attached a tcpdump taken from our edge during an affected window (helios_tcpdump_0803.pcap) and an exported route table.

From our initial look:
- traceroute to the connector IP sometimes shows a hop where packets appear fragmented and then stop responding
- we also observed ICMP unreachable (fragmentation needed) in a small sample set

We performed a maintenance window last night (03:00 local) which included a firmware upgrade on our F5 and a BGP soft-reconfig on the data center router. Could be related.

Can Redwood confirm whether any NAT or path changes were applied on the private connector side? We need to get an urgent call scheduled — production traffic is being affected.

Sam Carroll
Network Engineering
Helios Health

Attachments: helios_tcpdump_0803.pcap (pcap), helios_vpc_routes_0803.csv (csv)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carroll <sam.carroll@helioshealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

Thanks Sam — we see your packet capture and route export. I'm opening an internal triage and will loop in our networking folks. Initial asks while we pull logs:
- Can you confirm whether you observed asymmetric routing for client->Redwood vs Redwood->client? (traceroute from both sides helps)
- Do you have MSS/clamping configured on the F5? If so, what is the current value?
- If possible, run: sudo tcpdump -ni <edge-if> 'host <connector-ip>' and capture the first 60s of a failing flow and share.

I'll schedule a 60-minute session for tomorrow morning (Aug 4) to try live repro with your ops team.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, sam.carroll@helioshealth.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

Sam — quick preliminary notes after pulling connector logs and forwarding relevant bits from our edge:
- We see increased TCP retransmit counts and duplicated ACKs on inbound flows matching the windows you reported.
- Our VPN tunnel status shows frequent small BGP flaps between 02:55–03:10 (soft resets) correlating with your maintenance window. Logs attached: redwood_vpn_status_0803.txt
- There is a NAT gateway in the path for this deployment; the gateway config includes a connection tracking timeout of 60s for established flows and an aggressive port reuse policy. That can make long-lived flows brittle if there are mid-path changes.
- In a few samples, ICMP fragmentation-needed messages were generated but dropped before reaching the sender (we're seeing ICMP rate limiting at a hop).

Immediate mitigations we propose for the joint session:
1) Verify PMTU by enabling verbose traceroute and allowing ICMP type 3 code 4 on both sides.
2) Temporarily set TCP MSS clamp to 1350 on the F5 and our edge to avoid fragmentation.
3) If NAT-induced port churn is suspected, add a NAT bypass for the affected prefix pair during troubleshooting.

I'll bring packet captures and our kernel counters. Available to join the call tomorrow at 08:30 PT.

— Dev
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_vpn_status_0803.txt
From: Nadia Ruiz <nadia.ruiz@helioshealth.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: netops@helioshealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 07:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

Dev / Irene — following up with config snippets from our edge box. During the firmware upgrade we pushed a new fragment handling profile and reverted it at 04:10 after we saw increased retransmits. We also added a temporary ACL to block ICMP echo in the maintenance window (we realize now that may have been a mistake). Snippet attached: helios_edge_config_0804.txt

We can enable ICMP (type 3 code 4) if that will help. We can also schedule the cutover to the NAT bypass if you confirm the syntax you expect for the prefix exclusion.

— Nadia
Senior Network Engineer
Helios Health
Attachments: helios_edge_config_0804.txt
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sam.carroll@helioshealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 07:25 AM Nadia Ruiz <nadia.ruiz@helioshealth.com> wrote:
> Dev / Irene — following up with config snippets from our edge box. During the firmware upgrade we pushed a new fragment handling profile and reverted it at 04:10 after we saw increased retransmits.

Thanks for the details — dug into the captures and the kernel counters. Short analysis & recommended runbook for the joint session:
1) Evidence for PMTU blackhole: we see ICMP frag-needed (type 3 code 4) originating from mid-path but your ACL was blocking ICMP back to the sender which prevents PMTU correction.
2) MSS issue: several SYNs have MSS advertised at 1460 but actual payloads exceed the path MTU resulting in fragmentation attempts.
3) NAT behavior: the NAT gateway is performing port translation and connection tracking resets at ~60s which explains the resets for long-lived flows when route flap occurs.

Immediate step sequence (coordinated during the 60-min window):
- Helios: re-enable ICMP type 3 code 4 for the troubleshooting window.
- Helios: temporarily set F5 TCP MSS clamp = 1350.
- Redwood: add temporary NAT bypass rule for Helios source prefix -> connector destination (will avoid port churn while we monitor).
- Both: capture tcpdump simultaneously and run simultaneous traceroute with -M do and -f 1400 to confirm.

If that mitigates, follow-up actions: harden NAT session timeouts to 10 minutes for affected mapping, align MSS clamp on both edges, and schedule a maintenance window to coordinate a permanent route preference (BGP dampening/keepalive tuning) so soft-reconfigs don't break flows.

I'll be on the call tomorrow at 08:30 PT. Please confirm.

— Soojin
Senior Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carroll <sam.carroll@helioshealth.com>, Nadia Ruiz <nadia.ruiz@helioshealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures: packets dropped / high retransmits to private connector

Thanks everyone — joint window scheduled for Thu Aug 6 08:30 PT. Summary / immediate actions prior to the call:
- Helios will temporarily re-enable ICMP type 3 code 4 and enable MSS clamp = 1350 on the F5 during the session.
- Redwood will add a temporary NAT bypass for Helios prefix 10.22.0.0/18 -> connector IP range and hold NAT session timeout at 10m.
- Both teams capture simultaneous tcpdump and share to the doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-Helios-triage-notes
- HubSpot ticket created for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/cases/HELIOS-4521 (case HELIOS-4521)

Expected outcomes: validate PMTU path, confirm NAT bypass mitigates resets, and produce a remediation plan including a permanent configuration and a maintenance window.

I'll coordinate exec updates after the call. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

— Irene Choi

Redwood Inference
